title: Ember and Salt
premise: Odile Eriksen, runaway apprentice of a burned hedge-witch, hides her gift by keeping ledgers for the Saltglass Guild, which trades in impossible things: bottled grief, borrowed years, names cut loose from their owners. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, a dying guildsman sells her a secret — the king has been unmade and replaced by something wearing his shape, stitched together from stolen magic. Odile joins a ragged crew of hunted misfits who become the family she never had, and together they trace the usurper's power to its source. In the end Odile must choose between using the same corrupting magic to destroy it or unbinding herself, and she chooses to give up her own gift to free the broken king, finding that what she built with others outlasts anything taken alone.
about_author: Isandro Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant guild records in coastal port cities before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, power, and the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She balances the Saltglass Guild's books by candlelight, cataloguing traded wonders while hiding her own small gift of seeing what things truly are. A routine audit reveals an entry that shouldn't exist: a payment made in the king's own name for 'a crown's worth of quiet.' Emotional beat: wary contentment cracked by first unease.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Royal criers announce the Gift-Hunt: anyone with magic must register or burn. The guildmaster burns his most dangerous inventory overnight; a fellow clerk is dragged away screaming. Odile packs her mistress's old grimoire and runs. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Dying Man Sold
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Hunted through the dockside fog, she shelters with Tammas Vey, a guildsman bleeding out from a hunter's iron. He sells her his final secret for a promise: the king on the throne is not the king — something else wears him. Emotional beat: guilt and terrible inheritance.

chapters.title: A Crew of Ashes
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Fleeing the city, she falls in with three other hunted gifted: Brannic, a disgraced soldier whose strength is borrowed; Sefa, a child who speaks to drowned things; and Mother Quill, a forger of souls' names. Emotional beat: reluctant belonging beginning to take root.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Mother Quill's POV. The group travels a sentient old road that shows travelers their truest selves. It shows Odile her apprenticeship fire — and that she lit it. Emotional beat: shame confronted, trust tested among the found family.

chapters.title: Iron in the Wheat
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Hunters ambush the group at a farmstead. Brannic spends too much of his borrowed strength saving Sefa and collapses, revealing how little time he has left. Odile keeps them alive with ledger-logic, mapping the hunters' patrol patterns like accounts. Emotional beat: sacrifice, and Odile's value proven.

chapters.title: The Guild of Quiet Hands
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. They reach a hidden sanctuary of neutral guildsmen who trade in secrets. There Odile decodes Tammas's clue: the usurper draws power from a vault beneath the palace called the Emberhold. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Sefa Hears the Sea Count
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The child communes with drowned spirits who whisper that the thing in the crown was once a man — the king's twin brother, erased from every record. Odile realizes erasure is the usurper's method and weakness. Emotional beat: horror softened by compassion.

chapters.title: Mother Quill's Price
chapters.summary: Mother Quill's POV. To forge them court credentials, Quill must trade away a memory she can't spare — the face of her dead daughter. She does it without hesitation, and Odile understands the cost of the family forming around her. Emotional beat: grief as currency, love as debt.

chapters.title: Court of Paper Faces
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Disguised as a tax auditor, Odile enters the palace and stands feet from the king. Her gift shows her the truth: a hollowed man wrapped in something vast and hungry that notices her noticing. Emotional beat: terror laced with pity.

chapters.title: The Offer Wearing a Smile
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The usurper finds her privately and offers everything: safety for her friends, restoration of her gift's full power, a place at his side. He shows her what she could be. She refuses — but he lets her leave, and she knows why. Emotional beat: temptation and its corruption made intimate.

chapters.title: Fracture Lines
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. The group argues over Odile's report: fight, flee, or negotiate. Old wounds split them; Sefa runs into the night and is nearly taken. They recover her, but the family is cracked. Emotional beat: found family strained to breaking.

chapters.title: The Emberhold Below
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Guided by Sefa's drowned voices, they infiltrate the vault beneath the palace and find the source: the real king, alive but unraveling, his name and years siphoned to feed his brother's shape. Emotional beat: revelation and rising dread.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Borrowed Ink
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Their sanctuary contact sold their route to the crown weeks ago. Hunters flood the vault; Mother Quill holds the door with her last forged name and is captured. The survivors escape into the undercity. Emotional beat: betrayal, loss, and fury.

chapters.title: What Odile Lit
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Cornered and blaming herself, Odile confesses fully: the fire that killed her hedge-witch mistress was hers, born of fear of her own growing power. Brannic and Sefa choose her anyway. Emotional beat: confession met with grace — the theme of identity faced head-on.

chapters.title: The Unbinding Rite
chapters.summary: Mother Quill's POV (from captivity). Interrogated by the usurper, Quill stalls by teaching him false lore — and secretly passes the true rite of unbinding to Odile through a smuggled page: the binding can only be undone by someone willing to give up their own gift entirely. Emotional beat: defiance in chains.

chapters.title: Storming the Salt Gate
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. The city rises as the Gift-Hunt turns on ordinary folk too. Brannic spends the rest of his borrowed strength breaking Quill from the dungeons, knowing it will kill him. Emotional beat: heroic expenditure, farewell without goodbye.

chapters.title: The Throne Room of Two Kings
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Climax begins. Odile reaches the throne room where the usurper, crowned and colossal with stolen power, offers her partnership one final time. The wasted true king watches from the shadows. She begins the unbinding as the usurper tears the room apart. Emotional beat: courage against overwhelming corruption.

chapters.title: Ember and Salt
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Climax. The unbinding requires her to pour her own gift into the severed bond between the brothers. She does it — burning her magic out, naming the erased twin back into existence until the false crown crumbles to salt. The usurper ends not destroyed but remembered, and dissolves weeping. Emotional beat: self-sacrifice transfiguring power into mercy.

chapters.title: The King Who Came Back Small
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The restored king, diminished and human, ends the Gift-Hunt and asks Odile to help rebuild — not with magic, but with ledgers. Brannic survives, barely, emptied of borrowed strength but finally only himself. Emotional beat: exhaustion, tenderness, dawn.

chapters.title: New Entries
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Weeks later, the found family opens a small counting-house for the formerly hunted, recording names the crown tried to erase. Odile's gift is gone; in its place is only skill, memory, and the people beside her. Emotional beat: quiet joy, identity rebuilt without magic.

chapters.title: The Last Page of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Closing the first volume of the new house's books, Odile writes one final entry — the true account of everything that happened, including her own crime and forgiveness. She seals it, blows out the candle, and joins the noise of her family downstairs. Emotional beat: peace earned, story complete.
